title: Gideon and the Will
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Gideon is exhumed for a disputed insurance claim, Ulyana Villalobos discovers it empty — and realizes the 'death' forty years ago was a payout built on a lie. Using her photographic memory, she decodes a ledger disguised as hymn numbers in the church bulletin, revealing that Gideon faked his death to escape a crime, and that several founding families have been paying to keep the secret. At the anniversary dinner, Ulyana exposes the living Gideon — now the town's aged patriarch in plain sight — choosing truth over the loyalty of the community that raised her, and accepting that survival sometimes costs everything.
about_author: Coral Nakamura is a former claims adjuster from a small coastal town who writes mysteries about paperwork, memory, and the lies communities tell themselves. She lives quietly with two cats and an archive of obsolete insurance forms.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty
chapters.summary: Ulyana Villalobos, POV. Sent to verify remains for a contested policy, Ulyana witnesses the exhumation of founder Edmund Gideon and photographs an empty coffin. Her photographic memory catches a detail others miss: fresh soil layered over decades-old rot. The beat is cold professional curiosity curdling into dread as the town's reverence begins to feel like a wall.

chapters.title: Hymns in Numbers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Digging through archives, she recognizes the church bulletins' hymn selections form a numerical cipher matching entries in Gideon's original ledger — payments dated after his death. When someone ransacks her office, she understands the town's beloved families are complicit. The emotional beat shifts from investigation to isolation: knowing too much makes her a stranger.

chapters.title: The Man at the Head Table
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The cipher's final entry points to the anniversary dinner's guest of honor — Aldous Wren, Gideon's protégé and the town's patriarch, whose hands match a scarred man in a 40-year-old photograph. Confronted privately, Wren offers her a place among the protected if she stays silent. The beat is temptation: loyalty versus truth, survival offered at the price of her identity.

chapters.title: A Glass Raised to No One
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the dinner, with the ledger projected before the town, Ulyana names Wren as Gideon and lays out the fraud, the payments, the empty grave. The town fractures — some thank her, some never will. In the aftermath she declines a settlement, keeping only her memory and her name. The beat is costly resolution: truth chosen, belonging surrendered, survival redefined.
